title: The geometry of Floquet states
authors: Vladimir Y. Cherynak, John R. Klein
abstract: This paper studies the moduli space of "good" periodic Hamiltonians, i.e., periodic Hamiltonians with nondegenerate Floquet spectrum. The corresponding Floquet states determine a geometric model for the moduli space of such Hamiltonians. The model is expressed in terms of configuration spaces, flag manifolds, and principal bundles. A corollary of the main result is the complete determination of the rational cohomology ring of the space of good periodic Hamiltonians.   The paper also considers the adiabatic driving of a 1-parameter family of good periodic Hamiltonians. We formulate two conjectures describing the resulting asymptotic quantum evolution. These are Floquet analogues of the adiabatic theorem in quantum mechanics.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous geometric theory for the moduli space of quantum systems described by periodic Hamiltonians with non-degenerate spectra. It determines the topology of this space and formulates conjectures that provide an adiabatic analogue to the quantum mechanical adiabatic theorem. This work is significant for understanding the long-time, slow evolution of quantum states in periodically driven systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mathematical geometry and topology of the moduli space of periodic Hamiltonians that possess a non-degenerate Floquet spectrum.
main_result: It determines the rational cohomology ring of this moduli space and formulates two conjectures describing the asymptotic quantum evolution under slow adiabatic driving.
method: The analysis employs advanced concepts from differential topology, including the use of diffeological spaces, principal bundles, and the formulation of geometric analogues to the adiabatic theorem.
model_or_system: The system is quantum mechanics governed by time-periodic Hamiltonians, $h(t)$, analyzed via Floquet theory. The geometric structure is modeled using quasi-periodic states and associated bundles.
